sources.note: Casts benchmark contamination auditing as sparse-mixture detection, proves that detectability is governed by the single quantity alpha*rho*sqrt(m), and shows empirically that the resulting power predictions transport while the sample-size budgets derived from them do not.
sources.title: When Is Benchmark Contamination Detectable? Information Limits and Power-Calibrated Audits

sources.note: Calibrates feature-based data-contamination detectors against the systematic feature shifts that post-training introduces, by measuring how controlled prompt variants move scores on known non-members and then correcting only the recurring shift directions, with the gains concentrated at the low-false-positive operating point rather than in AUC.
sources.title: Calibrating Post-Training Feature Shifts for LLM Data Contamination Detection

sources.note: A benchmark where each task needs one commonsense step and one math step, on which model accuracy drops nearly 30% relative to solving the steps in isolation while humans show no such gap.
sources.title: AgentCoMa: A Compositional Benchmark Mixing Commonsense and Mathematical Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios

sources.note: Shows that benchmark contamination in reasoning models is alarmingly easy to hide: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals contamination detectors rely on, and PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the cause — implying a broad class of RL methods conceals contamination inherently.
sources.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models

result.definition: Deciding whether a particular example was in a model's training data, and across 4 sources the technical core of contamination auditing. The archive's results are mostly about the limits. Detectability is governed by a single quantity combining contamination fraction, effect size and sample count, and the resulting power predictions transport across settings while the sample-size budgets derived from them do not -- so an audit can be planned for power and not for cost. Post-training moves the features detectors rely on, which one source corrects by measuring how controlled prompt variants shift scores on known non-members and adjusting only the recurring shift directions, with the gains concentrated at the low-false-positive operating point rather than in AUC. And a brief round of reinforcement learning suppresses the signals outright, attributed to importance sampling and clipping rather than to any specific algorithm. The standing consequence is that a negative audit result on a post-trained model is close to uninformative unless its power was calculated in advance.
